title: bytes.len() as u64 cast: silent truncation on 32-bit targets (usize < u64)
description: blob.rs and client.rs: bytes.len() returns usize. The cast 'bytes.len() as u64' is safe on 64-bit targets because usize == u64, but on 32-bit targets usize is 32 bits. A body of more than 4 GiB would truncate silently. In practice reqwest will exhaust memory before returning a 4 GiB Bytes, so this cannot be triggered as written. However, the correct idiomatic cast is 'u64::try_from(bytes.len()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX)' or simply relying on the fact that the limit check itself prevents >limit bytes. This is at minimum misleading: the check 'if bytes.len() as u64 > download_limit' on a 32-bit target would silently pass for a body larger than u32::MAX, defeating the cap. The crate does not declare a 64-bit-only target requirement. File as correctness because it is a real bug on 32-bit targets even if the practical risk is low.
